newsitem.title: USA: Journalists to head Internet publishing startup.
newsitem.headline: Journalists to head Internet publishing startup.

text.p: New York Times columnist Peter Lewis and technology journalist and consultant Jim Seymour said Monday they will head an Internet startup next year that aims to create a new online market for information.

The company seeks to provide both original content and to re-publish research and creative works over the Internet, creating a library ranging from travel guides and recipes to market tips and sheet music, the journalists said.

The startup, known as ideaMarket, is based in Austin, Texas, where the journalists reside. It is among more than a dozen recent offspring of Idealab, a firm founded just nine months ago in Pasadena, Calif. by entrepreneur Bill Gross.
Seymour joins the company as president and chief executive officer and Lewis, who is due to step down at the Times this week, will serve as vice president and editorial director.
Lewis has been writing for the New York Times about the Internet for several year, work he said he considers to be "a dream job," but he was drawn by the opportunity to put his observations to work.
"This really brings into play all of the things I've been preaching over the last few years and I thought it was time to put up or shut up," he said in an interview.
